newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Chronology of events in Albanian pyramid scandal.
newsitem.headline: Chronology of events in Albanian pyramid scandal.

text.p: The collapse of get-rich-quick pyramid savings schemes which mushroomed in Albania after the overthrow of the communist regime in 1990 has sparked violent protests across the country.
Nine national investment schemes, some offering returns of more than 60 percent a month, have been set up over the past six years, sucking in millions of dollars of savings.
There are no official figures for the number of people involved but some estimates say 90 percent of the population has been drawn in.
Here is a chronology of the main events in the scandal.

Oct 7, 1996 - The World Bank and International Monetary Fund (IMF) urge Albania to impose strict controls on the so-called pyramid schemes. Some of the funds offer investors even higher interest returns in the wake of the IMF warning.
Nov 18 - Maksude Kademi, a 30-year-old gypsy known as Sude who headed one of the pyramid schemes, fails to make payments.
Nov 21 - The Albanian parliament votes to set up a committee to investigate the investment funds.
Nov 26 - Aleksander Grunasi, head of a pyramid scheme, vanishes with $13 million of savers' funds.

Jan 7, 1997 - Opposition parties accuse President Sali Berisha's ruling Democratic Party government of using the schemes to finance 1996 general and local election campaigns. The government rejects the charge as "vile slander".
Jan 15 - Hundreds of protesters demanding money back from Sude's pyramid scheme fight with riot police.
Jan 16 - The government seizes 25.5 billion leks ($255 million) deposited in state-owned banks by two of the schemes.
People in Vlore, 147 km (80 miles) west of Tirana, hurl stones at the city hall after a local firm postpones payments.
Jan 18 - President Berisha vows to crack down on pyramid schemes and warns the opposition not to use their collapse to destabilise the state.
Jan 19 - Some 3,000 Albanians, led by opposition party figures, break through police cordons to demonstrate in Tirana's main Skanderbeg Square.
Jan 21 - The Albanian government forms a commission to investigate the crumbling investment schemes.
Jan 22 - Thirteen people are sentenced to between one and two weeks in jail for taking part in the January 19 protest. A further 39 are fined 5,000-20,000 leks ($50-200).
Jan 23 - Parliament bans pyramid schemes and imposes a minimum jail term of 20 years for those trying to run them.
Hundreds of investors demonstrate in the northern city of Shkoder, others protest in the Adriatic port of Durres.
Jan 24 - Around 5,000 people go on the rampage in the southern town of Lushnje.
Jan 25 - Demonstrators attack Foreign Minister Tritan Shehu in Lushnje.

Jan 26 - Protests spread, sparking the worst violence seen in Albania since 1991. Thousands of people, accompanied by opposition party leaders, converge on central Tirana and clash with riot police. Government and Democratic Party buildings set ablaze in towns and cities across Albania.
An emergency sitting of parliament calls in the army to guard roads and government buildings.
Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi promises that investors in the pyramid schemes will get their money back from February 5.
Jan 27 - Democratic Party accuses leftwingers of inflaming the protests and calls for a counter-demonstration on Tuesday in front of the main opposition Socialist party headquarters.
